source.reason: Describes the homogenization heat treatment applied to the ingot prior to hot forging/solutionization; precursor to the MAF-1 state.

processing_steps_notes.value: Cast ingot of Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C (prepared by vacuum induction melting) homogenized at 1200 °C for 2 h before hot forging.

source.reason: Hot forging step applied to the homogenized ingot before solutionization; part of the thermo-mechanical history of the MAF-1 sample.

processing_steps_notes.value: Hot forged between 1200 and 900 °C ensuring more than 60% deformation with intermediate heating, then cooled by water quenching.

source.reason: The 1-pass MAF sample's parent process is the solutionized + water-quenched state; this step establishes the initial microstructure (50 μm grains, ρ0=0.79×10^15 m^-2) that is then warm-deformed.

processing_steps_notes.value: Forged material solutionized at 1050 °C for 1 h and water quenched to retain maximum austenite phase. This is the parent process (proc_solutionized-wq-1050c-1h) that yields the MAF-0 state before MAF.

source.reason: This is the defining processing step of the sample MAF-1 (1 pass): warm multiaxial forging at 250 °C with 33% normal strain per pass giving equivalent strain ≈0.47.

reduction_ratio.value: 33% normal strain in a single pass (equivalent strain ≈ 0.47)

processing_steps_notes.value: Warm MAF along three mutually perpendicular directions (one pass) on a 100-ton hydraulic press; 30×20×20 mm billet in a die with groove 32×20 mm; sample and die heated to 250 °C and soaked for two hours; ram speed 1 mm/s; samples lubricated with MoS2 before pressing. The 1-pass condition is denoted MAF-1.

source.reason: Consolidated microstructural description of the MAF-1 (1 pass) sample from XRD (crystallite size, microstrain, dislocation density), EBSD (grain size 35 μm, boundary fractions, texture/IPF) and KAM analyses.

overall_structure.value: Warm multiaxially forged (1 pass) Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C low-density steel: single-phase (majority austenite) FCC microstructure that is deformed and progressively subdivided, with a markedly increased dislocation density and changed preferred orientation relative to the solution-treated state.

region.value: Central analysed plate of the MAFed billet (location shown in Fig. 3a); normal/pressing direction probed by XRD/EBSD

morphology.value: deformed, elongated grains; grain subdivision with dense low-angle subgrain network

grain_size.value: 35 μm average (EBSD); average crystallite size 13.4 nm (XRD)

texture.value: changed from (111) in solutionized state to (220) preferred orientation; texture being broken up/randomized; many different crystallographic directions parallel to pressing direction

morphology.value: carbide reflections κ(220) and κ(222) present; unchanged before and after MAF

source.reason: Text states initial austenite grain size reduces to 35 μm after the first MAF pass; also marked in Fig. 8(b).

grain_size_distribution.value: Initial (MAF-0) distribution was relatively wide; after deformation the distribution becomes narrower/more uniform; MAF-1 area-fraction vs grain-size curve sits between MAF-0 and MAF-3.

texture.value: Solution-treated material was strongly textured with normal direction parallel to [101]; after 1 pass texture is randomized/broken up with many directions parallel to pressing direction.

source.reason: The MAF-1 sample is essentially single-phase austenite, so interfaces are grain boundaries and dislocation–boundary interactions; boundary fractions and twin fraction are explicitly reported for MAF-1.

coherence.value: grain boundaries characterized by misorientation angle; high-angle boundary (15°–180°) fraction 0.292, low-angle boundary (1°–15°) fraction 0.708

interaction_type.value: dislocation accumulation at low-angle subgrain/grain boundaries

qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: After 1 pass the low-angle boundary fraction increases drastically to 0.708 (from 0.367 in MAF-0) while the high-angle fraction falls to 0.292; a dense green low-angle subgrain network forms inside grains, reflecting heavy dislocation accumulation and subgrain subdivision.

slip_behavior.value: No deformation twinning occurs in this alloy; deformation proceeds by dislocation glide/accumulation (KAM average increases to 0.72°), with dislocation mobility and annihilation at grain boundaries suppressed at low temperature.

phase_evolution.value: No new phase forms during MAF; carbide reflections remain unchanged (no change in precipitation), and the strong initial texture progressively randomizes with pass number.

interface_notes.value: A negligible annealing twin boundary fraction of 0.007 is present in MAF-1. Grain boundary character in MAF-1 (Fig. 7b): low-angle 1°–15° = 0.708, high-angle 15°–180° = 0.292.

source.reason: The modified J-C model + FEA framework of the paper is applied to each MAF stage including MAF-1; the model constants (Table 4) and equations describe the numerical model, with validation against the MAF-1 experimental yield strength.

simulation_method.value: 3-D finite element analysis (explicit dynamics) of the MAF forging operation, incorporating the modified Johnson-Cook constitutive model

software_used.value: ABAQUS/Explicit with a user-material VUMAT subroutine

potential_model_or_database.value: Modified Johnson-Cook constitutive model (Eq. 6) with strain-dependent dislocation density (Eq. 7) and grain size (Eq. 8); J-C model parameters from the authors' previous study and Table 4.

boundary_and_initial_conditions.value: 3-D model 30 mm × 20 mm × 20 mm; die and punch discrete rigid bodies, workpiece deformable; mesh size 0.6 mm (41382 C3D8R hex elements, reduced integration with hourglass control); punch displacement 10 mm in Y (height); die fixed; material flow allowed only in X (flow direction) and constrained in Z by the die wall; friction coefficient 0.15; steady-state MAF simulated by mapping deformation fields from previous passes.

validation_against_experiment.value: Simulated dislocation density, grain size and flow stress compared with XRD (Fig. 5) and EBSD (Fig. 8) measurements at the Fig. 3(a) location. For MAF-1 the FE-simulated yield strength (dashed curve, Fig. 13) lies just below the experimental value (1040 MPa). Simulation predicted maximum central-region strain ≈0.6 after one pass, exceeding the applied external strain value of 0.46, in an X-shaped deformation pattern.

equation_role.value: Predicts flow stress incorporating grain-boundary strengthening (Hall-Petch) and dislocation (Taylor) strengthening added to the original J-C strain/strain-rate/thermal terms.

model_note.value: Eq. 6: σflow = (σ0 + k(df^-1/2 − d0^-1/2) + αMGb(ρf^1/2 − ρ0^1/2) + Bε^n)[1 + C ln(ε̇/ε̇0)][1 − ((T−Tr)/(Tm−Tr))^m]. Implemented via VUMAT with six state-dependent variables (SDV1–SDV6).

equation_role.value: Empirical saturating-exponential relation between imposed equivalent strain and dislocation density.

model_note.value: ρf = ρ0 + k1(1 − exp(−k2 ε)). For MAF-1, ε = 0.46, ρf measured = 5.57 × 10^15 m^-2.

equation_role.value: Exponential decay of grain size with imposed equivalent strain.

model_note.value: df = d0 exp(−k3 ε). For MAF-1, ε = 0.46, df measured = 35 μm.

unmapped_findings: For the MAF-1 sample the equivalent strain is reported as 0.46 in Table 1 (XRD-derived data) but as ≈0.47 in the process description text.
Average Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) value for MAF-1 is 0.72° (MAF-0 = 0.34°), indicating significantly higher local (stored) strain after one pass.
No deformation twinning occurs in this alloy during MAF; only a negligible annealing twin boundary fraction of 0.007 is present in MAF-1.
The MAF-1 billet survived one pass without fracture; the sample could only be forged a total of five times before breaking on the sixth attempt.
The tensile specimens for MAF-1 were cut from the located region of the MAF billet (Fig. 3a) with two specimens tested per pass to confirm reliability.

FE simulation for MAF-1 predicted a maximum strain of approximately 0.6 in the central region of the specimen, exceeding the applied external equivalent strain value of 0.46, in an X-shaped deformation pattern.
